qt: to the Commission Afroditi Latinopoulou (PfE) Subject:

According to Eurostat data for 2024, 21.9 % of people aged 16 and over in Greece who needed a medical examination or treatment said they were unable to obtain it due to cost, long waiting times or distance, compared to just 3.6 % in the EU. This is the highest rate among Member States and is around six times the European average. The Country Health Profile 2025 for Greece also highlights significant regional and income inequalities in access to care. In light of the above: Does the Commission consider that the reforms and investments financed by European funds, including the Recovery and Resilience Facility, have to date achieved a measurable improvement in citizens' access to health services?
